description:
The isolated capture phase runs AFTER all timed queries, on the measurement
connection. For read-only workloads this is exactly correct. But when the
workload MUTATES data during the run, the post-measurement capture sees the
POST-mutation database state, so the captured plan (and its cardinality
estimates / chosen join order) can differ from the plan the optimizer actually
chose when the query ran during measurement.

Concretely (verified 2026-06-15):
  - Standard power and throughput query sets are SELECT-only (TPC-H/TPC-DS
    permutations contain no DML), so no divergence there.
  - Maintenance tests (TPC-H RF1/RF2 inserts+deletes, TPC-DS data maintenance)
    and combined mode (power -> throughput -> maintenance) DO change table
    cardinalities. In combined mode the maintenance step runs AFTER the measured
    query phases, so a single post-run capture reflects post-maintenance data.
  - Any benchmark whose query set itself contains DML has the same exposure.

This was a non-issue while capture was inline (the plan was captured at the
moment each query ran). Moving capture to a post-measurement phase introduces the
divergence, so the canonical-isolation work must resolve it rather than silently
capturing a plan that never ran.

Options to evaluate:
  A) Capture-before-mutation: run the isolated capture pass at the point in the
     lifecycle BEFORE the first data-mutating step (e.g. before maintenance in
     combined mode), still outside any timed loop.
  B) Per-phase capture: capture once per measured sub-phase (after power, before
     maintenance) so each captured plan matches the data state it ran against.
  C) Documented read-only contract: capture only for read-only runs; for runs that
     mutate data, emit a clear warning that captured plans reflect end-of-run state
     (and/or skip capture for the mutating queries).
The chosen option must keep capture out of the timed window and out of concurrent
streams.

anti_patterns.dont: move capture back inside the timed loop to dodge this
anti_patterns.instead: solve it within the isolated-phase model.

anti_patterns.dont: silently capture a post-mutation plan for a query that ran against pre-mutation data
anti_patterns.instead: capture before mutation or label/skip it.
anti_patterns.why: the fingerprint then describes a plan that never executed

preserves.behavior: Capture stays outside the timed window and outside concurrent streams.
Read-only workloads keep capturing correct plans with no behavior change.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/integration/ -k 'capture and (combined or maintenance or mutation)' -v
verifications.description: Combined/DML run captures a plan matching the measured data state (or warns)
verifications.expected: captured plan matches measured-state expectation or documented warning fires

work_units.notes:
Enumerate the run shapes where the post-measurement DB state differs from the
measured state (combined mode, maintenance, DML-containing query sets). Quantify
whether captured fingerprints actually change for representative cases.
work_units.summary: Characterize divergence: which test types / benchmarks mutate data before capture

work_units.notes:
Choose per the trade-offs; coordinate with query-plan-capture-canonical-isolation
w3 (all-test-type coverage) since both touch where in the lifecycle the phase fires.
work_units.summary: Decide the resolution (before-mutation / per-phase / documented contract)

work_units.notes:
Add a test on DuckDB combined mode (or a DML-containing query set) asserting the
captured plan matches the data state it was measured against (or that the
documented warning fires and capture is skipped/labelled accordingly).

Related fidelity gap raised in PR #889 review (chatgpt-codex-connector, P2): the
phase records executed queries in _phase_recorded_queries keyed by query_id via
setdefault (benchbox/platforms/base/result_capture.py and execution.py). In
TPC-H/TPC-DS power/throughput the SAME query_id renders DIFFERENT SQL per
seed/stream (e.g. TPCHPowerTest derives seed + stream_id*1000 and passes
stream_id to get_query). With setdefault-by-query_id only the FIRST variant's SQL
is recorded, so _capture_plans_post_measurement captures one plan and attaches it
(plan + fingerprint + capture_time) to EVERY later row sharing that query_id —
rows that actually ran a different variant. While fingerprints still embed literal
values (query-plan-capture-fingerprint-literal-normalization is Not Started), those
attached fingerprints are wrong for the non-first variants.
This is PRE-EXISTING isolated-phase behavior (it already affects the originally
phase-eligible engines: DuckDB/MotherDuck/PostgreSQL/Redshift/SQLite/DataFusion);
the canonical-isolation cutover (PR #889) extended the same phase to the remaining
EXPLAIN engines per the ratified contract, so it now applies uniformly.
Resolution to evaluate (coordinate with the literal-normalization TODO): key
_phase_recorded_queries by concrete SQL (or (query_id, sql)) and attach captured
plans to result rows by matching SQL, so each row gets the plan for the variant it
actually ran — for ALL eligible engines, not just the ones added in #889.
Interim contract: under "capture once per query — a plan is a property of
(query, schema, engine)", once fingerprints are literal-normalized the structural
fingerprint is variant-stable and the attachment is correct; the per-variant
ANALYZE timing remains representative rather than exact.
work_units.summary: Preserve per-stream/seed query variants in the phase recording buffer
